correctness.rationale: Write U=G(x) where x=ξ·e. Each reciprocal power is strictly convex on [−1,1]. G′ is strictly increasing, G′(1)>0, and G′(−1)=0 exactly at p/(1−p)=A^k/B^k, equivalent to q_c=tanh((d+2)atanh r). The angular derivative vanishes at both poles and otherwise exactly at roots of G′. If G′(−1)<0 the poles are strict maxima and the unique interior critical coordinate is the global minimizing latitude, at two points on the circle and a (d−2)-sphere otherwise. If G′(−1)≥0 the profile is strictly increasing off the endpoint; the weak pole is a minimum, and is nondegenerate unless equality holds. The height difference has the sign of q. Solving G′=0 gives a−bx₀=2at/(1+t), a+bx₀=2a/(1+t); the terms combine as t^(k−γ)+1=1+t, yielding the stated valley value. The endpoint values follow directly, and inversion of the strictly increasing threshold gives the stated r_c and its dimension asymptotic. For δ=q_c−q, put D=cγb(A^(−k)+B^(−k))/2 and E=cγkb²(A+B)/(AB(A^k+B^k)); then G′(−1)=−Dδ and G″(−1) at threshold is E>0. The implicit root shift is (D/E)δ+O(δ²), the quadratic contrast is (D²/(2E))δ²+O(δ³), and 1−cos θ=θ²/2+O(θ⁴) gives the angular distance and the threshold term (E/8)θ⁴. These are the printed constants, at fixed d,r, and include p=1/2 and threshold equality. RESULT.md lines 66–106 are supported by this analytic reconstruction.
